question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?
answer:
The following parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" should be reviewed by a lawyer:

From Passage [1] and [2] (PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT):

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld."

- Definition of "Change of Control":  
'"Change of Control" shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement.'

- Additional provision:  
'...for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a "Party" in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the "Holder") of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates.'

Summary of review points:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires the express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- The definition of Change of Control includes sale/lease/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority ownership.
- Issuance of securities in a financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes transfer of more than 50% of voting stock.

A lawyer should review these provisions to assess:
- Whether consent is required for assignment upon Change of Control.
- The scope of what constitutes a Change of Control.
- The implications if the new controlling party is a competitor.
- Whether there are any exceptions or additional requirements (such as notice).

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control in the provided passages, but assignment restrictions and consent requirements are present.

Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

From Passage [1] and [2] (PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT):

- Section 20.4 Change of Control: 
  "Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. - Section 20.1 Assignment: 
  "No Party shall assign, license, transfer or change any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld conditioned or delayed; provided, however, that except as provided in Section 20.4 either Party may assign its rights hereunder to an Affiliate or to any successor by merger, consolidation, sale of stock or other equity interests or the sale of substantially all of the assets of such Party without the consent of the other Party."

Key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the agreement requires the express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- In other cases (not involving a Competing Product), assignment to an Affiliate or successor by merger, consolidation, sale of stock, or sale of substantially all assets does not require consent.
- The definition of "Change of Control" is broad and includes asset sales, mergers, and certain stock transfers.
- There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment restrictions and consent requirements apply in specific scenarios.

These sections should be carefully reviewed by a lawyer to assess the implications for both parties in the event of a Change of Control, especially regarding consent requirements and the impact of competing products.

From Passage [1] and [2] (PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT):

  "Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction.
